ei.title: Chapter 0-QN38-39 2번: Why Misprints Are Not Like Mutations
ei.subject: 올림포스9대변별유형

fullPassage: Misprints in a book or in any written message usually have a negative impact on the content, sometimes (literally) fatally. The displacement of a comma, for instance, may be a matter of life and death. Similarly most mutations have harmful consequences for the organism in which they occur, meaning that they reduce its reproductive fitness. Occasionally, however, a mutation may occur that increases the fitness of the organism, just as an accidental failure to reproduce the text of the first edition might provide more accurate or updated information. At the next step in the argument, however, the analogy breaks down. A favorable mutation is going to be more heavily represented in the next generation, since the organism in which it occurred will have more offspring and mutations are transmitted to the offspring. By contrast, there is no mechanism by which a book that accidentally corrects the mistakes of the first edition will tend to sell better.

questions.passage: Misprints in a book or in any written message usually have a (A)[negative / positive] impact on the content, sometimes (literally) fatally. The displacement of a comma, for instance, may be a matter of life and death. Similarly most mutations have (B)[harmful / beneficial] consequences for the organism in which they occur, meaning that they reduce its reproductive fitness. Occasionally, however, a mutation may occur that increases the fitness of the organism, just as an accidental failure to reproduce the text of the first edition might provide more accurate or updated information. At the next step in the argument, however, the analogy breaks down. A (C)[damaging / favorable] mutation is going to be more heavily represented in the next generation, since the organism in which it occurred will have more offspring and mutations are transmitted to the offspring. By contrast, there is no mechanism by which a book that accidentally corrects the mistakes of the first edition will tend to sell better.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 오식은 내용에 '부정적(negative)' 영향을, 돌연변이는 '해로운(harmful)' 결과를 낳지만, 때로 '유리한(favorable)' 돌연변이도 생긴다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① negative — harmful — favorable: 세 자리 모두 원문·문맥 일치 ←정답
❌ ② positive(긍정적인) — harmful — favorable: (A) 오식은 내용에 '부정적(negative)' 영향을 주므로 positive는 반대
❌ ③ negative — beneficial(이로운) — favorable: (B) 대부분의 돌연변이는 '해로운(harmful)' 결과를 낳음, beneficial은 반대
❌ ④ negative — harmful — damaging(해로운): (C) 적합도를 높이는 것은 '유리한(favorable)' 돌연변이, damaging은 반대
det.tip: negative(부정적) ↔ positive(긍정적), harmful(해로운) ↔ beneficial(이로운), favorable(유리한) ↔ damaging(해로운)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 돌연변이는 적합도를 '줄이지만(reduce)', 이따금 '높이는(increases)' 것도 있고, 책이 실수를 '바로잡는(corrects)' 경우다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① raise(올리다) — increases — corrects: (A) 돌연변이는 적합도를 '줄인다(reduce)', raise는 반대
✅ ② reduce — increases — corrects: 세 자리 모두 원문·문맥 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ reduce — decreases(줄이다) — corrects: (B) 이따금 적합도를 '높이는(increases)' 돌연변이가 생김, decreases는 반대
❌ ④ reduce — increases — worsens(악화시키다): (C) 책이 실수를 '바로잡는(corrects)' 상황, worsens는 반대
det.tip: reduce(줄이다) ↔ raise(올리다), increase(늘리다) ↔ decrease(줄이다), correct(바로잡다) ↔ worsen(악화시키다)

det.korean: '우연한(accidental)' 실패, 다음 세대에 '많이(heavily)' 나타남, 더 '잘(better)' 팔림 — 세 자리 모두 원문 일치.

questions.passage: Misprints in a book or in any written message usually have a negative impact on the content, sometimes (literally) fatally. The displacement of a comma, for instance, may be a matter of life and death. Similarly most mutations have harmful consequences for the organism in which they occur, meaning that they reduce its reproductive fitness. Occasionally, however, a mutation may occur that increases the fitness of the organism, just as an accidental failure to reproduce the text of the first edition might provide more accurate or updated information. At the next step in the argument, however, the analogy __________. A favorable mutation is going to be more heavily represented in the next generation, since the organism in which it occurred will have more offspring and mutations are transmitted to the offspring. By contrast, there is no mechanism by which a book that accidentally corrects the mistakes of the first edition will tend to sell better.
